chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from 'Ali from Abi Basir from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the price of wine, so he said: 'A rawiyyah (a specific measure/container) of wine was presented to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) after wine had been prohibited, so he ordered it to be sold. When the one selling it turned away with it, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called out to him from behind: O owner of the rawiyyah, indeed He who prohibited its drinking has prohibited its price.' So it was ordered to be poured onto the ground, and he said: 'The price of wine, and the dowry of the prostitute, and the price of the dog that does not hunt from game.'

key_terms.رَاوِيَةٌ: A specific measure or container of wine

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the price of wine in Shia jurisprudence according to the Prophet's practice?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* elucidates the principle of *thaman al-khamr* (price of wine), establishing that the prohibition of consumption inherently extends to its monetary value, a ruling derived from the Prophet’s specific instruction to sell it and then nullify the transaction. It categorically groups the price of wine with the dowry of a prostitute and the price of a non-hunting dog as *mal al-khabith* (good wealth), reinforcing the concept of *fasad al-aqd* (invalidity of contract) due to the intrinsic impurity of the commodity. This hadith is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between mere prohibition of use and the broader economic invalidity of the item's exchange value.
